_exec_summary.SummaryText:
ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION POLICIES
Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility has a long-standing commitment to worker and public safety. This commitment is demonstrated by the resources invested in accident prevention, such as personnel training and consideration of safety in the design, operation, and maintenance of the sulfur dioxide process.  Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility's policy is to implement reasonable controls to prevent foreseeable releases of regulated substance.

STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCE
Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility is located at 27400 Avenue 6, Madera, California.  The regulated substance managed at the facility is sulfur dioxide.  At most, nine (9) one-ton cylinders are kept on-site for a total of 18,000 pounds (lbs.).  

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM
As part of the implementation of this CalARP Program, key Prevention Program elements were documented and implemented by Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility to manage process safety issues associated with the use of sulfur dioxide.  Furthermore, common industry standards, policies, and procedures are currently utilized to ensure safe practices are being performed. The regulated substance is over the 500-lb. state threshold for CalARP Program.  As a result, the sulfur dioxide covered process is subject to CalARP Program 3.

HAZARD ASSESSMENT SUMMARY/OFFSITE CONSEQUENCE ANALYSIS

Worst-Case Release Scenario Results Summary
One (1) worst-case analysis has been defined and modeled for the sulfur dioxide process.  The results are in the most recent Hazard Assessment documentation.

Alternative Release Scenario Results Summary
An alternative release scenario was modeled and the results are in the most recent Hazard Assessment documentation.

Risk Considerations
Although the storage and use of sulfur dioxide has inherent potential risks, and worst-case release scenarios can potentially reach the community; Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility has recognized these potential risks and structured its safety pr

ograms to make the worst-case type of event non-credible.  In addition to the safety practices of the company and plant personnel to make this worst-case event non-credible, it should also be recognized that there are inherent analysis assumptions that make the results of the atmospheric dispersion analysis appear worse than what would actually be expected during such event.

In addition to the use of conservative analysis assumptions that over-predict the effects of a potential release, other characteristics of the facility and site serve to minimize the potential risks associated with a sulfur dioxide release such as having process valves to permit isolation of any leaks in place; scheduled maintenance to reduce the likelihood of catastrophic failures; Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) used by facility personnel, as necessary; a well-designed relief system; gas detection systems and alarms; and safety showers/eyewash stations.

FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility has had no releases in the last five (5) years that meets the five-year accident history reporting criteria. 

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
Sun-Maid Ripperdan - Facility is a non-responding facility and does not train employees for active responses to sulfur dioxide releases.  This facility will rely upon the local emergency hazardous materials response team and the local Fire Department for responses to uncontrolled releases of sulfur dioxide.  The facility is not required to have an Emergency Response Plan in place.  However, it is required to have appropriate mechanisms in place for notifying emergency responders when there is a need for response.  These mechanisms are described below. 
 
The Facility submits a Hazardous Material Inventory (HMI) Business Plan via California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) as necessary.  The Facility has procedures in place to evacuate the facility and notify responders when there is a need for a response.  A current copy of the Emergency Acti

on Plan (EAP) is with the Safety Manager.

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
Several studies have been conducted to examine mitigation measures to improve safety at the facility.  These studies include the Process Hazard Analysis (PHA), Hazard Assessment, and Compliance Audit performed as part of the prevent program requirements. Any outstanding recommendations from these studies are addressed per regulatory requirements.

EXTERNAL EVENTS ASSESSMENT
Pursuant to the requirements of California Code of Regulations, general events external to the plant that can conceivably cause a release of sulfur dioxide are addressed in the PHA.  The assessment includes a description of the types of natural and human caused external events, an estimated magnitude or scope of external events , the magnitude of the external events, and recommendations as necessary.

Human Factors are discussed in the PHA, which also include; major hazards identified, process controls in use, mitigation systems in use, and monitoring and detection systems in use.
